summary.headline: APSEZ Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% to INR11,340 crore and EBITDA 23% to INR6,807 crore; FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance raised by INR1,000 crore each.
summary.overview: Management reported broad-based growth across domestic ports, international ports, logistics and marine, with consolidated revenue up 24% YoY and EBITDA up 23%. FY27 guidance was raised to revenue of INR44,000-46,000 crore and EBITDA of INR26,000-27,000 crore, and FY27 capex guidance was increased by INR3,000 crore, mainly for Indian ports. International ports had a record quarter with EBITDA more than tripling, while marine was hit in July-August by Strait of Hormuz disruption that left vessels idle. Management said domestic volumes were already growing double digits in October after a weak Q1 caused by the Middle East crisis, iron ore export curbs and coastal coal timing.

segments.name: Domestic ports
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13% YoY with a 72.5% EBITDA margin. Mundra ran at about 91-92% average utilisation in Q1-Q2, with some terminals above 100%.

segments.name: International ports
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,839 crore (+71%) and EBITDA INR878 crore, margin 47.7%. CWIT Colombo handled 2 million TEUs in 18 months and its capacity is being doubled from 1.6 to 3.2 million TEUs; Tanzania posted its highest-ever container volume.

segments.name: Logistics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 21% YoY. Truck revenue up 28% YoY and integrated freight network revenue more than doubled. Container volumes rose 15% QoQ in Q2 after the Q1 slowdown.

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: Revenue up 57% and EBITDA up 32% YoY, with fleet at 138 vessels. Margin fell QoQ in July-August as about 7-8 Astro offshore vessels were stranded by the Strait of Hormuz closure; management said margins recovered from September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR44,000-46,000 crore (up INR1,000 crore).
FY27 EBITDA guidance raised to INR26,000-27,000 crore (up INR1,000 crore).
FY27 capex guidance increased by INR3,000 crore, all in India (Mundra, Dhamra, Hazira, Vizhinjam); management said no international capex is included.
Management declined to derive a full-year EBITDA margin from the guidance range, calling H2 an assumption rather than arithmetic.
Vizhinjam Phase 2 delivery committed for December 2028. Possible 1 billion tonne capacity a little before 2031 if the current pace continues.
Management expects the transshipment mix at Mundra to return to 20-22% after CT5 starts; CT5 was due to start within weeks.
capex_capacity: Domestic capacity target raised to 1 billion metric tonnes, with Mundra, Vizhinjam, Dhamra, Kattupalli and Ennore in expansion; 18 MMT Paradip expansion completed.
CT5 at Mundra to start in a few weeks, already contracted for volume and revenue; management said it missed some capacity opportunity during the Q1 disruption.
CWIT Colombo capacity doubling from 1.6 to 3.2 million TEUs; Colombo Phase 2 expected to be settled over the next two or more quarters.
Vizhinjam Phase 2 delivery committed for December 2028; the EXIM yard at Vizhinjam has seen strong traction.
Vadhvan HAM bid for reclamation and nearshore development: no visibility on award; first work targeted 2028 or 2029.
More than INR30,000 crore capex deployed over the past 2 years.
demand_pricing: Container volumes at Mundra were running above 800,000 TEUs in August, with October running close to that level; management said domestic volumes were already growing double digits as of 28 October.
Iron ore exports at Dhamra were hit by the export ban; coking coal volumes were said to be growing on contracts and higher steel demand; coastal coal is the key focus for the next two quarters.
Liquid cargo market share gained significantly; Hazira handles more than 140 liquid types.

Management said the India market share (about 27% for 2.5 years per an analyst) was depressed by one-off STS cargo at anchorages during the Hormuz closure, and asked analysts to adjust the denominator.
Management did not quantify the INR depreciation impact on India port EBITDA; it said the effect was positive for revenue composition.
Colombo outperformance came from automation and efficiency, with volumes above expectations at lower unit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in logistics, and is double-digit growth sustainable? Why would the full-year EBITDA margin fall to about 58.5% on the revised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said logistics growth is structural, driven by ICD ramp-up (Virochannagar, Malur) and the integrated multimodal model; it said guidance is a hypothesis, not arithmetic, and asked analysts not to derive a 58.2-58.5% margin from it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex raised, and are international acquisitions on the radar?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex increase is India-only, accelerated for Mundra, Dhamra, Hazira and Vizhinjam because Mundra was at 90-92% utilisation and CT5 was coming. Management is evaluating more than 20 international assets against four tests: top/bottom-line growth at or above APSEZ's, geopolitics and macro, financing, and a leadership partner.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international EBITDA margin to 47.7%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Colombo was the main driver, as an automated terminal with higher volumes and lower cost; Australia also contributed. Management said Australia's margin should stay within 1-2 points, Haifa is unlikely to improve, and it needs two more quarters before giving entity-level guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did marine margin fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Astro offshore vessels (7-8 on standby) could not transit the Strait of Hormuz in July-August, leaving war insurance and fixed costs without revenue; margins improved from September as transits resumed.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a Mundra disruption from local yard operators' strikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an empty-yard issue had been resolved: 120 acres of empty yard are now inside the port and full, with another 200 acres planned, plus an integrated warehouse.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Indian market share flat, and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was not normal: container volumes were hit by the Middle East crisis and dry cargo by policy; October is recovering, and it expects market share gains in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Visibility of Mundra transshipment mix returning to 20-22% once CT5 starts, and of CT5's ramp.
Marine utilisation depends on Strait of Hormuz transits; a fresh closure would repeat the July-August hit.
Colombo Phase 2 commissioning to 3.2 million TEUs, and the international margin trajectory for Haifa, Tanzania and Australia.
Iron ore export policy and the discharge-side share of coastal coal, which management flagged as a structural issue.
Vizhinjam stake sale timeline, which management said is on track but depends on signing; Vizhinjam Phase 2 due December 2028.
Market share data: management argues the all-India denominator is distorted by STS cargo, which makes the market share trend hard to verify.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and growth, with a clear stance that the Q1 weakness was temporary. Evasive on margin and international specifics: it declined to give a full-year margin and asked analysts to wait for Q3-Q4 and more quarters for entity-level international margins.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CT5 at Mundra starts within weeks and is already contracted for volume and revenue; Mundra runs at 91-92% utilisation with some terminals above 100%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Mundra containers were above 800,000 TEUs in August with October close to that; management says domestic volumes were growing double digits as of 28 October after a weak Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR44,000-46,000 crore and EBITDA to INR26,000-27,000 crore (each +INR1,000 crore), but management called H2 an assumption rather than arithmetic.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic volume recovery, CT5 and the raised guidance, but declined to derive a full-year margin and deferred on international margin specifics; analysts pressed on the implied 58.2-58.5% logistics-led margin and on the marine and Indian market share trend.

quality.why: Consolidated revenue +24% and EBITDA +23% are driven by domestic ports (+13%), international ports (+71% revenue, EBITDA more than tripled on Colombo automation and efficiency) and logistics (+21%), with no acquisition or accounting one-off stated; however, international growth is from a small base and the brief gives no volume growth figure for the quarter, and the marine hit is a profit drag rat
